content.text: While you can change your username later, doing so will break existing repository links. Therefore, it is highly recommended to choose a professional and permanent username from the start.
If you decide to change your GitHub username in the future, any active GitHub Pages URLs will change immediately. This will make your previous links invalid and inaccessible.

GitHub Pages uses a standard naming convention to create URLs directly from your username and repository (folder) name: `https://username.github.io/repository-name`.
For example, if you use JohnDoe as your username and project1 as your repository name, the URL will be `https://JohnDoe.github.io/project1`.
**However, there is an exception:** if you use your username as your repository name, the URL will be `https://JohnDoe.github.io`.
**Recommended Practice:**

items: **Your Personal/Academic Website:** For your primary website, it is recommended to use a repository named the same as your username. This gives you a cleaner, shorter URL: `https://username.github.io`.
**Project Websites:** If you create separate websites for specific projects, they can live under your main domain: `https://username.github.io/repo-name`.

content.text: **Note on Professionalism:** If your username is informal or difficult to spell, your professional academic website URL will inherit those traits. For example, `https://JohnDoe.github.io` is generally preferred on an academic CV over `https://techcoder99.github.io`.

I recommend using your personal email address. It ensures long-term ownership of and access to your account regardless of your institutional affiliation.
On the other hand, if you use an institutional address, you may need additional verification to prove your academic status.
